newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sells 10 bln dong T-notes, rate 10.99 pct.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sells 10 bln dong T-notes, rate 10.99 pct.

text.p: Vietnam sold 10 billion dong ($893,734) worth of one-year Treasury notes with an annual coupon of 10.99 percent to a domestic institution at an auction on Wednesday, an official at the State Bank of Vietnam said.
The sale was the first of the year and the first to find a buyer since November 27 last year when the central bank sold 2.5 billion dong worth of six-month bills at a rate of 8.20 percent.
The issue date of the notes sold on Wednesday is February 21 and maturity will be on February 21, 1998.
The bank said the allotment was sold to the Bank for Foreign Trade of Vietnam (Vietcombank). No other institutions took part in the auction.
A State Bank official said on Monday that a target interest rate for the sale had been set at 11 percent.
Treasury analysts indicated earlier in the week that the target rate might be deemed unattractive because of a recent decision to withdraw a tax exemption on interest income from treasury paper.
